title: Car Shipping in Schenectady, NY | Big Apple Car Shipping
metaDescription: Car shipping in Schenectady, NY from our Franklin Street office. Open and enclosed carriers for GE transfers, Union College and Florida. Call (518) 855-3097.
heroSub: Door-to-door Schenectady auto transport dispatched from 670 Franklin Street, a short walk from Proctors. GE and Knolls transfers, Union College move-outs, retirees to the Gulf coast and short hauls to Boston.
intro:
Car shipping from Schenectady is a job we dispatch from inside the city, not from a call center that thinks Schenectady is a suburb of Albany. Our office is at 670 Franklin St #605, Schenectady, NY 12305, downtown a block or two from Proctors Theatre, and the local line is (518) 855-3097. The Stockade is a few blocks west of us, Mohawk Harbor and Rivers Casino are a short drive up Erie Boulevard, and the Amtrak station is a short walk. This is the city that lit and hauled the world, and much of it still moves cars because of that history.

Schenectady auto transport runs on a handful of corridors the carriers already know: I-890 through the GE campus, I-90 at Thruway Exits 25, 25A and 26, Route 5 along State Street, Route 7 to Niskayuna and Troy, Route 146 to Clifton Park and Altamont Avenue out through Rotterdam. We book open and enclosed trucks for GE Vernova engineers transferring to Greenville or Houston, Union College families at move-out, Knolls Atomic Power Lab staff, Ellis Hospital hires, and retirees headed to The Villages who are done shoveling a Mont Pleasant driveway.

sections.h2: Where a carrier can and cannot load in Schenectady
sections.html:
The Stockade is the oldest residential neighborhood in the state, and its streets were laid out for carts, not 75-foot car haulers. Front Street, Washington Avenue, Union Street below Erie Boulevard and the lanes around Riverside Park are off limits to a full-size rig. If you live there, we meet at the Amtrak station lot on Erie Boulevard or in a Price Chopper plaza, and the whole handoff takes ten minutes.

Downtown is similar. Jay Street is pedestrian, State Street near Proctors is busy on show nights, and the garages do not clear a loaded trailer. In Hamilton Hill, Vale and Goose Hill, drivers usually ask for a cross street on Albany Street or Brandywine Avenue instead of the one-way blocks.

The easy pickups are the GE Realty Plot and Upper Union Street, where lots are wide and the corners are generous, and the suburban towns. Niskayuna, Rotterdam, Glenville and Scotia driveways on Route 7, Route 50, Route 5S and Curry Road are loaded at the house most of the time. For everyone else, the standing meeting points are Mohawk Commons on Balltown Road, the ViaPort Rotterdam lots that most people still call Rotterdam Square, and the big Mohawk Harbor lots by the casino, which have room to turn a full rig around.

sections.h2: GE, Knolls and Union College are why Schenectady ships cars
sections.html:
General Electric built this city and the move patterns still follow the company. GE Vernova's power business and GE Research on River Road in Niskayuna move engineers constantly, and the destinations repeat: Greenville, South Carolina for gas turbines, Houston for energy, Cincinnati for aviation, plus people coming the other way into the Capital Region. Relocation packages often cover one vehicle and leave the second to the family, so many of our GE calls are for the spouse's SUV that needs to arrive the same week as the household goods.

Knolls Atomic Power Laboratory in Niskayuna and the Navy nuclear training pipeline behind it send people on fixed orders to Charleston, Norfolk, San Diego and Bremerton. These are date-driven moves, so we book early and schedule pickup for the last working day.

Union College sits right between Downtown and the GE Realty Plot, and the campus does not have a loading zone for haulers. In mid-May and late August we run parent cars to and from Nott Street at the Amtrak lot or Mohawk Commons, and we ship graduates' sedans to Boston, New Jersey and the DC area. Ellis Hospital on Nott Street hires residents and traveling nurses on short notice, and that produces one-car moves in both directions all year.

sections.h2: How Schenectady auto transport actually gets routed
sections.html:
Most Schenectady loads do not originate here. A carrier is usually working the I-90 Thruway between Buffalo and Boston or coming up I-87 from the city, and Schenectady is a stop. Exit 25 at I-890 and Exit 25A at I-88 are where the driver comes off; Exit 26 serves Rotterdam and Scotia. That helps price, because a truck headed to Boston or the Carolinas already has a reason to pass through, and it is why the driver gives a two-day window rather than a clock time.

Southbound cars to Florida and the Carolinas typically ride I-87 to the Thruway and down I-81 or I-95, with transit of four to six days. Westbound to Texas, Arizona and California, the truck usually runs the Thruway to I-90 or drops to I-80 through Pennsylvania. Short hauls to Boston go straight out I-90 and can be a one-day job if the truck is already positioned near Albany.

On booking we ask for the real location of the car, whether it starts and steers, and a backup contact. A car at the GE Main Plant gate on Erie Boulevard, one in a Rotterdam driveway and one in a Stockade garage are three different dispatch jobs.

sections.h2: Retirees, snow and the Mohawk River
sections.html:
Schenectady retirees have a pattern: the house in Bellevue or Woodlawn sells, the move is to Florida's Gulf coast, Fort Myers, Sarasota, Naples or The Villages, and the car goes on a truck instead of making a 1,300-mile drive down I-95 at the end of October. We ship a lot of single cars out of Niskayuna and Glenville in late fall and return cars in April. Against two nights of hotels, fuel and tolls, the price gap is smaller than most people expect.

The river matters too. The Stockade and lower Front Street have a long history of ice-jam flooding when the Mohawk backs up in late winter, and the 2011 Irene flood put cars underwater in Rotterdam Junction and Scotia. We can ship a car that has been in water and repaired; the carrier just needs to know ahead of time if it does not start.

On the other end, plenty of four-season people leave Schenectady for the Adirondacks, Saranac Lake, Old Forge and Lake Placid, and want the second car or the sled trailer vehicle delivered rather than driven up Route 30 in a storm. Those are short hauls that a regional carrier handles in a day.

sections.h2: Open or enclosed on a Capital Region winter road
sections.html:
Nine out of ten Schenectady cars go open, and that is the right call for a Honda, a Subaru or a pickup. The Thruway and I-890 are heavily salted from Thanksgiving through March, so an open car leaving in January will arrive with brine on it; that is cosmetic, and a wash on the other end fixes it. Enclosed costs roughly 40 to 60 percent more and we recommend it for three situations: a car coming out of the GE Realty Plot that costs more than the house it is parked at, a classic going to a show or auction, and a Union College student's first car that a parent wants to arrive untouched.

Enclosed rigs are also smaller and can get closer to the Stockade and downtown than a ten-car open hauler, so some customers pick enclosed for the access as much as the protection.

sections.h2: Shipping a car to the port for family in Guyana or the Caribbean
sections.html: Schenectady has one of the largest Guyanese communities in the country, concentrated in Hamilton Hill, Mont Pleasant and along Albany Street, and a steady number of residents buy a used car here to send to family in Georgetown, Trinidad or Jamaica. We handle the domestic leg: the car goes from your street or a Price Chopper lot to the ocean freight forwarder's yard in New Jersey, Brooklyn or Baltimore, with a signed inspection report at both ends. You or your freight forwarder book the ocean portion and the customs paperwork; we do not export the vehicle ourselves, but we will coordinate the drop so the car arrives when the yard is open. For a running sedan, the Schenectady-to-port move is usually a one or two day job on an open truck.

faqs.q: I live in the Stockade. Can a truck pick up on Front Street or Washington Avenue?
faqs.a: No, and no honest dispatcher will promise it. The Stockade streets are too narrow and the turns too tight for a loaded hauler. We meet you at the Amtrak station lot on Erie Boulevard, which is a five-minute walk, or at the Mohawk Harbor lots. Smaller enclosed rigs can sometimes reach Union Street near Erie Boulevard, but not the interior blocks.

faqs.q: GE is moving me to Greenville. How far ahead should I book the second car?
faqs.a: Give us seven to ten days. Greenville is a common lane from Schenectady because of the turbine business, so carriers headed down I-81 and I-85 pass through regularly. We usually schedule pickup for your last day or two in town, often at Mohawk Commons or your Niskayuna driveway, and the car lands three to four days later, close to when the moving van does.

faqs.q: My son is at Union College. Can you pick up on campus at move-out?
faqs.a: Not on campus itself; Union does not have a hauler-friendly loading spot and the streets around Nott and Seward are packed in May. We set the pickup at the Amtrak station lot or Mohawk Commons on Balltown Road, usually the morning after finals. Parents who want the car to arrive clean typically take enclosed for a student car going to Boston or New Jersey.

faqs.q: I take Amtrak to Florida every winter. Can the car leave before I do?
faqs.a: Yes, and that is the standard setup for retirees in Bellevue, Woodlawn and Glenville. We pick the car up a few days before your Empire Service or Lake Shore Limited departure, you leave a key with a neighbor or hand it to the driver at the station lot, and the car is waiting in Fort Myers or The Villages when you arrive. Returns in April work the same way.

faqs.q: I bought a car in Rotterdam to send to my family in Guyana. Which part do you handle?
faqs.a: We handle the United States leg only: the pickup at your house, the ViaPort lot or the dealer, and delivery to the freight forwarder's yard in New Jersey, Brooklyn or Baltimore. Your freight forwarder books the ocean portion and the customs filing. Tell us which yard and its receiving hours and we will time the drop; it is usually a one or two day job on an open carrier.
